mcqs.question: Two features give slightly different splits under Gini impurity vs entropy. What should you conclude?
options: Gini and entropy usually produce very similar splits in practice, so this is expected and not a bug
One of the two impurity measures must be implemented incorrectly
You must always use entropy since it's mathematically more rigorous
The tree can't be trained until you pick a single impurity measure and validate it against ground truth
mcqs.explanation: Gini and entropy both peak at maximum class mixing and hit 0 at purity, so they usually agree on splits closely, with only minor differences. Neither is more 'correct' — Gini is just cheaper to compute (no logarithm) and is the common default.

mcqs.question: A decision tree has zero training error but poor validation accuracy. Which single change is most directly responsible for fixing this?
options: Switching from Gini impurity to entropy
Constraining depth or minimum leaf size so the tree stops fitting individual training points
Increasing the max depth to let it separate the remaining validation points
Standardizing the input features before training
mcqs.explanation: Zero training error with poor validation accuracy is the signature of overfitting — the tree grew until it memorized training noise. Depth/leaf-size limits directly address that. Impurity measure choice barely affects this, increasing depth makes it worse, and trees don't need feature scaling at all.

mcqs.question: Your features have a genuine interaction — the effect of income on approval depends on age — and you haven't engineered an interaction term. Which model captures this automatically?
options: A linear regression model, since it can adapt to any relationship given enough data
A logistic regression model with regularization
A decision tree, since each split's threshold can depend on the path taken through prior splits
Neither model can capture interactions without manual feature engineering
mcqs.explanation: A tree splits on age first, then can split on a different income threshold within each age branch — interactions fall out of the recursive structure for free. Linear and logistic regression assume additive effects and need an explicit interaction term (e.g. income × age) to represent this.

mcqs.question: A colleague reports 99.8% training accuracy from an unconstrained decision tree and wants to ship it. What's the right response?
options: Ship it — high training accuracy is the goal
Switch to entropy instead of Gini to reduce overfitting
Retrain with a smaller training set to reduce overfitting risk
Check validation/test accuracy first — an unconstrained tree likely memorized training noise
mcqs.explanation: Near-perfect training accuracy from an unconstrained tree is a red flag for memorization, not a sign of quality — you need held-out validation accuracy to know how it actually generalizes. Shrinking the training set doesn't fix overfitting, and the impurity measure has essentially no effect on this.
